A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Depth Any Video. All 14 pages of each version are readable, including equations, six tables, seven figures, and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, and no material gap limits comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video depth-estimation experiments, efficiency measurements, component ablations, and VAE reconstruction comparisons in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4, Tables 2–6, and the corresponding figures.

M1.justification: The SVD-based model, conditional flow-matching objective, frame dropout with RoPE, video packing, and key-frame-conditioned interpolation remain unchanged. Section 2 expands documentation of data collection and curation without establishing that the underlying procedure changed.

E1.justification: Both use DA-V, Hypersim, and Virtual KITTI 2 for training and the same image benchmarks, ScanNet++ video benchmark, and qualitative scenarios. v2 names Cities: Skylines II and Grand Theft Auto V as DA-V sources; this clarifies existing data provenance rather than establishing added coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 2–4 and Figures 4–5. Table 3 retains NVDS, ChronoDepth, and DepthCrafter; Table 4 retains Marigold, ChronoDepth, and DepthCrafter. The VAE comparison also retains the same models.

E3.justification: The zero-shot affine-alignment protocol, AbsRel/δ1/TAE metrics, 98 ScanNet++ clips of 32 frames, training budgets, and inference settings remain identical. The newly stated 30-FPS collection rate documents DA-V rather than revising a previously reported experimental setting.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 retains the same component ablations, denoising-step and ensemble-size sweeps, training-epoch analysis, and VAE reconstruction study. Tables 5–6 and Figures 6–7 add no analysis or experimental variant.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point estimates, averaging descriptions, and prediction-ensembling settings. Neither reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–6, plotted ablation results, and qualitative evaluation examples remain unchanged. For example, Table 3 reports Depth Any Video's ScanNet++ AbsRel of 9.3, δ1 of 93.4, and TAE of 2.1 in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same normalization, flow-matching formulation, interpolation conditioning, and temporal-alignment-error definition. The new rendering-pipeline overview is explanatory prose; no mathematical definition, derivation, assumption, or proof changes.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the dataset contribution: the introduction emphasizes a feasible scalable collection pipeline and synthetic-to-real generalization, replacing the first-dataset claim. Section 2 also removes the largest-dataset claim. The model contributions, supported input capabilities, and state-of-the-art performance claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 2 newly identifies menu switching as a source of image–depth misalignment and qualifies game-content use and sharing with non-commercial-use and spoiler restrictions. Interpretations of experimental performance and the stated limitations concerning reflections and extremely long videos remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands the previously generic DA-V collection documentation: ReShade depth extraction, synchronized OBS capture, named game sources, UI-removal plugin, manual scene filtering, collection by 10 players over two weeks, and 30-FPS recording. The abstract also newly states that code and model weights are open-sourced. These are substantial reproducibility disclosures; the PDFs do not independently verify resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 newly acknowledges Richter et al. (2016) and Krahenbuhl (2018) as precedents for collecting supervision from games, accompanying the narrowed dataset novelty claim. References to ReShade, OBS, and game-content policies are added. The broader related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in the introduction's synthetic-data discussion and Section 2, which gains a rendering-pipeline overview. There are also terminology, author-footnote, and bibliographic-style edits. Section order and most method and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 2–3 replace illustrative RGB/depth sequences while preserving their schematic structure. Table 5 corrects the duplicated 'Synthetic Synthetic Data' heading. Added prose shifts text and some display positions, but the overall layout and experimental figures and tables remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes DA-V's provenance and collection process substantially more transparent and places the dataset contribution more carefully relative to prior game-data work. It also documents usage constraints and reports code/weight release. These provide clear benefits to reproducibility documentation and claim precision, while the empirical evidence remains unchanged and details such as filtering thresholds remain unspecified.
